concept_definition: Having no value, effect, or significance; void.
Existing in a state of complete disorder and confusion; lacking organization or control.
Not connected, joined, or sharing a common part; separate.
Firmly fixed, steady, and unlikely to move, change, or fail.
Lacking the ability or strength to move or act; motionless and inactive.
Containing people or animals living in it; inhabited.
Characterized by or having a large amount of rain; wet because of rain.
Occupied and lived in by people or animals.
Affected or changed by the actions, ideas, opinions, or presence of someone or something.
Changed or modified to suit a new purpose, situation, or environment.
Affected by a disease-causing organism, such as a virus, bacterium, or fungus.
Abnormally or medically increased in size, especially of a body organ, tissue, or anatomical structure.
Not cooked, heated, or otherwise prepared for eating.
Caught and held, especially by force or after pursuit.
Kept in prison or another place of confinement as punishment or while awaiting trial.
Chosen or assigned to a position, role, task, or time by an authority or formal decision.
Made less strong, powerful, or effective; suffering reduced strength or effectiveness.
Contained as part of a whole, group, or set.
Having used all of something, especially money, energy, or time; exhausted or depleted.
Provided with the tools, equipment, or other things needed for a particular purpose or activity.
Functioning or working, especially as intended.
Meeting the necessary conditions or requirements for something, such as participation, selection, or a benefit.
Not valid, correct, acceptable, or legally effective.
Having an immune-system reaction to a particular substance, usually causing symptoms such as sneezing, itching, or swelling.
Not inhabited; having no people living in it or on it.
Forced to leave a country or place and forbidden to return.
Made impure, unsafe, or unfit for use by contact with a harmful or unwanted substance.
Changed or modified in order to improve, correct, or update something.
Limiting or controlling what someone can do or what is available; imposing restrictions.
Able to be obtained, used, bought, or accessed.
Established again after having ended, been interrupted, or been lost.
Having a climate or environment that is very dry but receives more precipitation than an arid environment, typically supporting grassland or sparse vegetation.
Absent or unavailable to such an extent that it can effectively be treated as not existing.
Able to provide everything one needs without help or support from others.
Included as a permanent part of a structure, system, or device rather than added separately.
Containing everything needed for its operation or use, without requiring outside help, equipment, or resources.
Involving or characterized by a high level of pressure, stress, or urgency.
Kept in good condition and not damaged, decayed, or changed despite being old or exposed to time.
Still in good physical condition and appearing youthful or healthy, especially despite age.
Capable of causing death; posing a serious risk to a person's life.
Fully developed, established, or qualified; having all the attributes, responsibilities, or status expected of the type.
Destined to have bad luck or an unfortunate outcome; doomed to fail or end badly.
Chosen, accepted, or enforced by oneself rather than imposed by another person or outside authority.
Involving a burn that affects only the outermost layer of the skin.
Free from ice; not covered or blocked by ice.
Partly independent; having some autonomy while still being subject to the control, support, or authority of another person or organization.
Able to continue or function without outside help, support, or supplies.
Made in advance and available for immediate use, rather than needing to be made or prepared specially.
No longer existing because the species, group, language, practice, or other thing has become extinct.
Involving the second level of seriousness or severity, especially a burn that damages the outer layer of skin and part of the layer beneath it.
Needing or wanting to drink because of a lack of water in the body.
Covered with or characterized by clouds; overcast.
Neat, orderly, and free from clutter or mess.
Filled with or obscured by fog; having reduced visibility because of fog.
Busy doing things; involved in or participating in activities, rather than idle or passive.
Of meat, especially beef, cooked only briefly so that the inside remains red and lightly warm.
Of farmland, left unplanted for a period so the soil can recover.
In health care, describing an illness, symptom, or condition that is not severe or intense.
Protected in a digital information system against unauthorized access.
Beaten or stirred until smooth, thick, or fluffy, especially with butter, sugar, or cream.
Slightly wet, usually from liquid or moisture, but not thoroughly soaked.
No longer fresh or recently made, especially of food; often dry, hard, or unpleasant to eat.
Cooked by being exposed to hot water vapor.
Heated until browned or crisp, especially by exposure to dry heat.
Growing older or showing the effects of age.
Neat, sharp, and freshly pressed, especially of clothing or paper.
Extremely bad, dangerous, or difficult; showing little chance of improvement or success.
Less strict or demanding than before; allowing more freedom or flexibility.
Changed from its original or proper state so that it is damaged, spoiled, or unusable; especially, data or a file that has been altered or damaged.
Not working or being used; inactive or available for use.
Clean, orderly, and arranged carefully; not messy.
Caught or confined so that escape or movement is difficult or impossible.
Taken out or removed from a place, account, or supply.
Having formally left or ended participation in an activity, competition, organization, or place.
Cut or otherwise separated from something, especially by a sharp or forceful action.
Worn, faded, or in poor condition from age or use; looking neglected.
Having had the skin removed, especially from a person or animal, or from fruit or vegetables.
Not interrupted, disturbed, or interfered with; left in peace or allowed to continue without interruption.
Not moved, altered, or touched; remaining in its original or natural condition.
Not changed, affected, or disturbed; remaining in its original condition.
Not used, consumed, or handled; left as it was.
Not harmed, damaged, or affected by something harmful; unharmed.
Extremely dry, with little or no rainfall; especially describing a climate or region.
In a natural or raw state, not refined, processed, or purified.
Having a fault, flaw, or imperfection that makes something not work properly or not meet the required standard.
Older in age or having lived longer, especially in comparison with another person or member of a family.
Not complete or fully developed; lacking some part or quality needed for completeness.
Not having all the parts, items, or information that should be present; not complete.
Not finished or fully carried out; still in progress or left unfinished.
Not damaged, broken, or harmed; remaining whole and in good condition.
Remaining complete or unchanged, especially as a whole or system; not diminished, removed, or altered.
Alone, with no other people or things present; isolated.
Remaining the same; not altered, modified, or different.
Captured and held prisoner, or kept confined and unable to leave.
Compelled to receive or use something because there is no practical alternative; having a restricted choice.
Dressed or covered in a particular kind of clothing or material.
Wearing clothes; dressed.
Restricted or limited by rules, circumstances, or a lack of freedom or resources.
Empty of people and lacking signs of life or activity; bleak and deserted.
Having been cleared or emptied by a flow of water, especially a toilet that has had its contents removed by flushing.
Containing or covered with mud; dirty or wet with mud.
Having one or more holes made through the body, especially the ears, so that jewelry can be worn.
Brought under control or made less powerful, intense, or active.
Not broken, damaged, or separated into pieces; still whole and intact.
Continuous, with no interruption, gaps, or breaks.
Not known or recognized by someone; not previously encountered.
Not completed, finished, or brought to the intended state.
Not fully developed, processed, or given a final surface treatment; especially of material or a product that has not undergone its final finishing.
Not occupied or being used; empty, especially of a place, room, or position.
Very old and deserving respect, especially because of its long history or traditional importance; sometimes used with affectionate or humorous irony for an old object or building.
Having an area of damaged skin or tissue that is discolored after being struck or squeezed, usually without the skin being broken.
Having bugs or defects, especially in computer software or electronic equipment.
Temporarily inactive or not growing, while capable of becoming active again; often describing a plant, animal, disease, or process.
Not currently active, operating, or being used, though still existing or available.
Not practiced or used for a long time, and therefore less skilled or effective than before.
Not influenced or changed by something; remaining as before despite its effects.
At a point of severe danger or illness, with the possibility of death or serious deterioration.
Made worse or more serious, especially by adding to an existing problem or injury.
Extremely cold; icy.
Remaining after the greater part has been used, removed, or dealt with; left over.
Of or relating to something that is fixed, stationary, or not changing.
Likely to change suddenly and unpredictably, especially in a way that could cause trouble or danger.
Having declined from a higher or more desirable condition, quality, or standard; deteriorated.
Remaining unchanged in value, form, or condition; not varying.
Empty or containing no writing, marks, or other content; not filled in or completed.
Slightly wet, especially in a way that feels unpleasant or is not fully dry.
Free from war, violence, or fighting; characterized by peace.
Calm and quiet, with little disturbance or activity.
Having become unpleasant or unsuccessful; characterized by deterioration or failure.
Available because it is not being used, occupied, or needed.
Filled with a prepared mixture, especially before cooking; often used of poultry, vegetables, or pasta.
Different from what is usual, expected, or considered normal; especially in a way that is unusual or concerning.
Worn smooth or bare through use, especially of a tire or a patch of ground.
Covered with or containing dust; not clean or recently used.
Having no home or permanent place to live.
Decayed or decomposed, especially through the action of bacteria or fungi; no longer fresh or sound.
Quiet, inactive, and lacking excitement or activity.
Covered with snow or receiving a great deal of snow.
Characterized by frequent or heavy snowfall; having a climate or season in which much snow falls.
Affected or afflicted by something harmful, distressing, or disabling, such as illness, fear, grief, or poverty.
Damaged or afflicted by a disaster, calamity, or other destructive event.
Owing more on a loan or other debt than the current value of the asset securing it, especially a home or vehicle.

concept_definition: Not having a paid job, especially while seeking work.
Marked by a physical blemish or imperfection, especially in a surface or material.
Not staying the same in behavior, quality, or results; varying or changing from one occasion to another.
Not wearing any clothes; naked.
Working and ready to be used; functioning as intended.
Harmed or impaired physically, so that something is broken, weakened, or no longer in good condition.
Harmed in a way that weakens a person's reputation, confidence, relationships, or prospects.
Characterized by constant change, activity, or progress; energetic and continually developing.
Old or fairly old, especially when referring politely to people; often used for people who are past middle age.
Cooked in hot oil or fat, typically until browned or crisp.
Damaged or rendered unusable by excessive heat, electrical current, or intense activity.
Difficult to endure because it is severe, extreme, or unpleasant, especially of conditions or circumstances.
Harmed physically, especially as the result of an accident, attack, or other event.
Harmed or damaged in a way that is not necessarily physical, such as having one’s reputation, feelings, or interests adversely affected.
Fully developed and ready to be eaten, especially of fruit or vegetables.
Fully developed or mature and ready for a particular event, condition, or use.
Ready or likely to experience something, especially an unpleasant event or consequence.
Extremely unpleasant, harmful, or severe; often used for conditions, weather, or pain.
Not existing or available; missing from something where it would ordinarily be found.
Wearing clothes, especially clothes of a particular kind or in a particular way.
Regular and secure, especially in reference to work, income, or a romantic relationship.
Bare, bleak, or devoid of vegetation or other visible life.
In poor condition, damaged, or in need of repair or financial help.
Suffering from a dangerous or urgent problem and needing help; in distress.
Wearing old, torn, or shabby clothes; looking untidy and poor.
Clear and calm, especially of weather, the sky, or a place; free of clouds or disturbance.
Left unable to leave or continue a journey, often because of a lack of transportation or help.
Separated or isolated from a group, support, or the usual surroundings; left alone without the means to get back or reconnect.
Not married; not having a spouse. Can describe a person who has never married or is currently not married, including someone who is divorced or widowed.
Having won a contest, battle, election, or other competition; having defeated an opponent.
Not yet used, altered, or explored; in a natural or original state.
Unrefined or untreated, especially describing oil that has not been processed or refined.
No longer alive; dead.
Not clean; dirty, soiled, or containing dirt or other unwanted matter.
Not hygienic or sanitary; likely to spread disease or otherwise harmful to health.
Having lived for a relatively long time; old.
Having been allowed to mature for a period of time, especially to develop flavor or quality.
Having reached a specified age or stage of development.
Not wearing clothes; uncovered by clothing.
Without a covering, coating, or protective layer; exposed.
Without disguise, concealment, or protection; openly exposed or unadorned.
Existing in fact or practice, even if not officially recognized or legally established.
existing by law, whatever the practice
